title: Markets & Prices: Final Assessment
description: This final assessment checks the key ideas from all three lessons. If you reach the passing score, you complete the course.

questions.prompt: The price of coffee beans has risen sharply. Other things being equal, what happens in the market for coffee drinks?

choices.text: The demand curve shifts to the right
There is a movement up along the supply curve
The supply curve shifts to the left
The demand curve shifts to the left

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a change in quantity demanded?

choices.text: A trend fades, so people buy less at the same price
The population grows, so people buy more at the same price
Incomes fall, so people buy less at the same price
The good's own price falls, so people buy more of it

questions.prompt: In a market with the supply function Qs = 10 + 2P, production costs rise, and quantity supplied falls by 6 at every price. What is the new quantity supplied at P = 20? (Enter a number only.)
The price is below equilibrium, so there is a shortage (excess demand). Without government intervention, how is the price likely to move next?

choices.text: Buyers accept higher prices, so it rises toward equilibrium
Sellers cut prices further to reduce the shortage
It stays where it is even as the shortage continues
The supply curve shifts right, and the shortage disappears

questions.prompt: A market has the following quantities at each price. Price 15: quantity demanded 75, quantity supplied 35 / Price 20: quantity demanded 70, quantity supplied 50 / Price 25: quantity demanded 60, quantity supplied 60 / Price 30: quantity demanded 50, quantity supplied 70. What is the equilibrium price? (Enter a number only.)
If the government sets a price floor above the equilibrium price, what is a likely result?

choices.text: Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, causing a shortage
Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, causing a surplus
The quantity traded rises above the equilibrium quantity
The equilibrium price falls to the level of the floor

questions.prompt: A market has the demand function Qd = 110 − 2P and the supply function Qs = 20 + P (equilibrium P = 30, Q = 50). A price ceiling of 27 is imposed. What is the deadweight loss? (Enter a decimal.)

Hypothetical example: When the ticket price for a show rose from $80 to $100, daily ticket sales fell from 200 to 170. Using the midpoint method, find the price elasticity of demand (absolute value), rounded to two decimal places.

An amusement park lowered its admission price, and the number of visitors rose by a much larger percentage than the price fell (demand is elastic). What happened to the park's total admission revenue?

choices.text: The price fell, so total revenue decreased
Price and quantity changed by the same percentage, so total revenue stayed the same
More tickets were sold, but each was cheaper, so total revenue decreased
Quantity rose by a larger percentage than the price fell, so total revenue increased

questions.prompt: In a country where food demand is inelastic, a poor harvest reduces supply. Which statement best describes a policy of giving low-income households direct help with food costs?

choices.text: It targets households in need, but with supply unchanged it adds upward price pressure and has fiscal costs
It lets supported households buy more food, so the market price tends to fall over time
It shifts the supply curve to the right, so the effect of the poor harvest largely disappears
It works much like a price ceiling, so it tends to create a shortage in the food market
